title: CINTAA faces contempt proceedings over October 20 elections; Bombay High Court seeks explanation
raw_summary:
The Bombay High Court has sought an explanation from the Cine and Television Artistes Association (CINTAA) over its decision to hold elections and announce the results despite earlier court directions, as per a report by Times Now. The development follows a contempt petition filed by the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE), which has accused the association of disregarding judicial orders.

On October 22, Justice Aarti Sathe issued a show cause notice to CINTAA, stating that the material placed before the court indicated a prima facie case of wilful disobedience and breach of undertaking. The court has also restrained the association from implementing the outcome of the elections held on October 20, 2026.

FWICE’s petition alleges that CINTAA failed to comply with directions issued by the Bombay High Court on September 11 and October 19. The earlier orders required the parties involved in the dispute to refrain from taking further steps that could affect the court’s directions while a Notice of Motion remained pending before the trial court.

According to the petition, CINTAA went ahead with its election process and declared the results despite these restrictions. FWICE has therefore approached the High Court seeking action over the alleged non-compliance. The federation was represented by Advocates Saveena Bedi Sachar and Ashok Shetty.

The show cause notice, issued under Rule 9(1) of the Contempt of Courts (Bombay High Court Rules, 1994), requires CINTAA to explain why proceedings under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, should not be initiated against it. The allegations concern the purported disregard of the previous orders and/or a wilful breach of the undertaking given before the court.

The High Court’s direction means CINTAA cannot act on the October 20 election results or give effect to them while the restraint remains in place. The notice represents an opportunity for the association to respond to the allegations; the court has not yet made a final determination on the contempt petition.

The matter is scheduled to come up before the Bombay High Court again on November 18, 2026.

title: Alia Bhatt, Sharvari-starrer Alpha to premiere on Sony MAX at 8 PM on October 31
raw_summary:
Alia Bhatt and Sharvari-starrer Alpha is set to have its World Television Premiere on Sony MAX on October 31 at 8 PM. Directed by Shiv Rawail, the film also features Anil Kapoor and Bobby Deol in pivotal roles. The film follows two women in the world of action and espionage, with Alia Bhatt playing an assassin trained to kill. The television premiere will allow viewers to watch the film at home during the festive season.

Speaking about the television release, Alia said she was glad the film would reach a wider audience beyond theatres. “With its television premiere on Sony MAX, Alpha gets to reach audiences in a whole new way. We put a lot of thought and energy into the action, the characters and the emotional journey of the film, so it’s exciting to see that journey continue beyond the theatres and into people’s homes,” she said.

The actor also spoke about the appeal of watching films with family during the festive season and the opportunity for Alpha to find new viewers. “The festive season is a wonderful time for films to become part of family movie nights. For those who haven’t seen Alpha yet, this is their chance to experience it and for those who have, perhaps a reason to come back to it,” she added.

Alia said it was encouraging to see a film continue to reach audiences after its theatrical run. “As an actor, it’s a wonderful feeling when a film continues to find new audiences, and I’m glad Alpha now gets to do that with Sony MAX,” she said. Sharvari on Alpha’s television premiere Sharvari also expressed excitement about the film reaching viewers through television. The actor said the project had been a significant experience for her, particularly because of its action sequences and emotional elements. “Alpha has been such an exciting and special journey for me, and seeing it now make its way to television feels incredibly rewarding. We put so much into the action, the emotions and the world of the film, so it’s exciting to know that it will now reachK audiences in a completely new way,” she said.

Sharvari added that watching the film at home could offer audiences an opportunity to share its action and emotional moments with their families. “There’s something particularly special about watching a film like Alpha at home during the festive season, where the big moments, the action and the emotions can be shared with family. Sony MAX has always had a way of bringing larger-than-life cinema into people’s homes, and I’m thrilled that Alpha gets to be a part of that,” she said.

The actor also hoped that both first-time viewers and those returning to the film would enjoy the experience. “I hope audiences who are watching it for the first time have as much fun with the film as we did making it, and that those who’ve already seen it find something new to enjoy this time around,” she added.

Alpha will premiere on Sony MAX on October 31 at 8 PM.

Shah Rukh Khan and Deepika Padukone are set to reunite on the sets of King for a grand song sequence that will be filmed in Mumbai from October 26, according to a report by Variety India. The song is expected to feature the film’s cast, with choreographer Vaibhavi Merchant overseeing the sequence. Preparations for the shoot are currently underway.

The film is backed by Gauri Khan, Siddharth Anand and Mamta Anand under the banners of Red Chillies Entertainment and Marflix Pictures.

title: No football, no gym, no restaurants? Tiger Shroff shooting raises a FRIGHTENING question: Are Bollywood stars becoming PRISONERS of their own fame?
raw_summary:
For Tiger Shroff, playing football has always been more than just a recreational activity. The actor, known for his extraordinary fitness and athletic abilities, has frequently been spotted enjoying the sport with friends.

On Sunday, October 18, he was doing precisely that. It was supposed to be another ordinary evening. Tiger had finished playing football at a ground in Juhu and was preparing to leave when unidentified assailants opened fire near his vehicle. Tiger escaped unhurt, but his driver and a bystander were injured.

The incident has understandably raised questions about Bollywood’s security arrangements, the threats faced by prominent actors and the possible involvement of organised crime. But there is another question that deserves serious consideration.

What happens when even the simplest activities in a Bollywood star’s life become potential security risks? And, perhaps more importantly, what does this mean for the culture of celebrity photography that has become an inseparable part of Bollywood?

Imagine being unable to step outside your home without planning your movements, checking security arrangements or wondering whether somebody is watching. For most people, playing football, visiting a gym, meeting friends at a café or going out for dinner are ordinary activities. For celebrities, however, even these moments have increasingly become public events.

The irony in Tiger’s case is particularly striking. Here is an actor whose entire professional identity revolves around strength, agility, martial arts and performing extraordinary action sequences. On screen, he regularly overcomes seemingly impossible situations. Yet the real-life incident occurred after something as simple as a football game.

The contrast is unsettling. No amount of physical fitness or martial arts training can eliminate the dangers posed by armed violence. And if an actor begins to feel that an ordinary football outing requires extensive security arrangements, the implications extend far beyond one individual.

What happens to the freedom to live spontaneously? Will actors eventually have to give up activities they have enjoyed for years? Will they have to restrict their movements to private facilities? Will something as simple as meeting friends require advance security coordination?

There was a time when seeing a film star outside a cinema screen was a relatively rare experience. Today, celebrity sightings have become an entertainment industry of their own. From airport arrivals and gym entrances to restaurant exits and family outings, virtually every movement of a major star is social-media content.

Consider a typical paparazzi video. It may reveal where an actor exercises, which restaurant they frequently visit, when they leave home or the route they routinely take. Individually, these details may appear harmless. But when repeated over weeks or months, publicly available information can reveal patterns. In Tiger’s case, investigators have reportedly examined whether the attackers had studied his movements and were familiar with his football routine.

There is no established evidence that paparazzi photographs or videos helped the attackers. It would be unfair and irresponsible to suggest otherwise. Nevertheless, the incident raises a legitimate question: Should Bollywood reconsider how casually the precise locations and daily routines of celebrities are shared?

After an incident as serious as the Tiger Shroff shooting, perhaps this relationship needs to evolve. The solution cannot be to blame photographers for criminal acts they did not commit. Nor should it involve unreasonable restrictions on legitimate journalism. However, it may be time for the industry to distinguish between photographing a public appearance and making someone’s private movements unnecessarily predictable.

There is another possible consequence. If security concerns intensify, celebrities could become increasingly inaccessible. Actors may begin using private entrances, travelling in secured vehicles, avoiding public recreational facilities and limiting informal interactions with fans. Even occasions that currently feel spontaneous could become carefully managed appearances.

In one sense, heightened security may be necessary for individuals facing credible threats. But it could also change Bollywood’s culture.

The most important aspect of this debate is perhaps the least visible. Security isn’t merely about employing guards or installing surveillance cameras. Living under a credible threat can affect an individual’s everyday choices and sense of independence. Ordinary pleasures may require careful planning. Family outings could become complicated. Even familiar environments might begin to feel less comfortable.

Psychologists who work with people exposed to violence often discuss how traumatic incidents can lead to heightened vigilance, anxiety and changes in behaviour. This does not mean Tiger Shroff is experiencing any of these reactions. His personal response is private, and it would be inappropriate to speculate.

But it highlights the broader human cost that can accompany serious security threats. Celebrities may enjoy extraordinary privilege, wealth and public admiration. Yet those advantages cannot fully compensate for the loss of personal freedom.

And that raises a deeply uncomfortable question about the future of celebrity life. If even an ordinary football game becomes a security concern, what happens to the freedom that the rest of us take for granted?

Bollywood’s stars may belong to millions of fans on the big screen. But surely, beyond the cameras, they deserve the freedom to live their own lives.

title: Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein revival in the works? Jackky Bhagnani reportedly in talks with Nitin Kakkar
raw_summary:
Could Maddy and Reena return to the big screen? More than two decades after Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein (2001) arrived in theatres, the romantic drama continues to find an audience through television re-runs and digital platforms. Now, according to industry buzz, producer Jackky Bhagnani is exploring the possibility of reviving the film’s universe, with filmmaker Nitin Kakkar reportedly being considered to direct the proposed project.

According to sources, discussions are underway between the makers and Kakkar regarding his potential involvement. The filmmaker is known for directing films such as Filmistaan, Mitron and Jawaani Jaaneman. He is also associated with the upcoming film Awarapan 2. However, the nature of his reported discussions with Bhagnani remains unclear, and there has been no official announcement confirming his appointment.

Details about the proposed Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein project are also under wraps. It remains to be seen whether the makers are considering a direct sequel that continues the stories of the original characters or a contemporary reimagining that revisits the film’s romantic setting and themes. The production house has not officially confirmed the project, its cast, the status of the script or a potential filming schedule.

Why Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein Continues to Find an Audience

Directed by Gautham Vasudev Menon, Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein introduced R. Madhavan and Dia Mirza to Hindi cinema, with Saif Ali Khan playing a pivotal role. The film revolved around the complicated romantic equation between Madhav Shastri, popularly known as Maddy, Reena Malhotra and Rajeev Samra, also known as Sam.

Although the film’s initial theatrical run did not immediately establish it as a major success, it gradually developed a dedicated following over the years. Its emotional conflicts, dialogues and music composed by Harris Jayaraj contributed to its continued popularity among audiences.

The film’s enduring presence in popular culture has kept interest in its characters alive, making the possibility of a revival a subject of discussion among fans. However, whether the proposed project will bring back the original characters or introduce a new story remains to be seen.

For now, the reported discussions are at a preliminary stage, and further details about the project are awaited.

title: Aamir Khan says, ‘Rajkumar Hirani will narrate 3 Idiots sequel’s final script in the coming weeks’

Aamir Khan has shared a fresh update on the much-awaited sequel to 3 Idiots. The actor confirmed that director Rajkumar Hirani is currently working on the script and is expected to narrate the final version to him in the coming weeks.

Aamir shared the update while attending the Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF), where he received the Screen Icon Award. Before speaking about the project, the actor checked with Hirani about whether he could reveal the latest development.

“Well, I’m not allowed to say a lot. I think I can say this much, that yes, Raju is working on the script. In fact, hopefully once I’m back in the next couple of weeks, he’s going to narrate the final version to me. So, fingers crossed,” Aamir said.

title: Abundantia aiON, in partnership with InVideo, announces its first film Beta Builder
raw_summary:
Abundantia aiON, the AI-powered creative studio division of Abundantia Entertainment, in partnership with AI video technology company InVideo, today announced its first film Beta Builder. It’s a part of a three-film slate backed by an Rs. 100 crores joint corpus between Abundantia aiON and InVideo. The film is based on author Sukriti YJ’s novel ‘Beta Builder: Mumbai In The Metaverse’.

Beta Builder tells the story of Jai, a self-taught, genius architect from Dharavi who gets a chance to realise his dreams in the virtual reality world, only to discover that winning means far more than just proving himself. An underdog in every sense, Jai must fight the system that holds him back, win the love of his life, and give his community a voice in shaping its own future. Rooted in one of India's most iconic neighbourhoods and set against the limitless possibilities of a virtual world, Beta Builder is a story about ambition, belonging and what it truly means to build something that lasts.

The film is being developed and produced under Abundantia aiON's 'Human-First, AI-Empowered' creative philosophy, one that places human authorship and storytelling vision at the centre while harnessing AI across the production value chain, from development to screen.

Announcing the project, Vikram Malhotra, Founder and CEO of Abundantia Entertainment, said, “Beta Builder is everything aiON was built for, a story that begins in one of Mumbai's most iconic neighbourhoods and travels into a world that does not yet exist, told through technology that is rewriting what filmmaking can be. Jai's journey is about ambition, identity and the courage to build something bigger than yourself. It is a deeply human story, and the fact that it is being brought to life through AI makes it even more exciting to us. This is what Human-First, AI-Empowered means in practice. And this is just the beginning of what aiON and InVideo will build together."

Beta Builder is the first in a slate of five AI-driven films being developed by Abundantia aiON in partnership with InVideo over the next three years. The broader aiON slate will span fully AI-generated features as well as live-action and AI hybrid productions, with titles beginning to roll out from the first quarter of 2027.

Founded in 2013, Abundantia Entertainment's filmography includes Baby, Airlift, Toilet: Ek Prem Katha, Shakuntala Devi, Sherni, the Chhorii franchise, Breathe, Daldal, Subedaar and Maa Behen.

title: Madhur Bhandarkar announces Syama – The Missing Chapter on Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee
raw_summary:
Filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar is set to explore the life and legacy of Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee in his next project, following the completion of his upcoming film The Wives of Bollywood. The National Award-winning filmmaker and Padma Shri recipient will direct the film, which is backed by producer Aditya Kumar Halwasiya and jointly produced by Bhandarkar Entertainment and AKH Ventures.

Titled Syama – The Missing Chapter (working title), the film aims to bring the story of Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee to the big screen, revisiting his political journey, ideological beliefs and role in India's history.

A scholar and statesman, Dr. Mukherjee was a prominent political figure who advocated national unity. His journey included becoming the youngest Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta and serving in independent India's first Cabinet under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

The film will explore his ideological differences with the government, his decision to resign from the Cabinet and his role in founding the Bharatiya Jana Sangh in 1951. It will also revisit his 1953 campaign against the permit system in Jammu and Kashmir and the circumstances surrounding his death in detention.

Combining elements of historical drama and political thriller, Syama – The Missing Chapter seeks to examine the decisions and convictions that shaped Dr. Mukherjee's public life. The project also aims to revisit a chapter of India's political history and introduce his ideas and legacy to a new generation of viewers.

Speaking about the project, producer Aditya Kumar Halwasiya said, “Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee’s life is a powerful reminder that true leadership lies in courage, conviction and service to the nation. Through Syama, we aim to bring his remarkable journey to the screen and inspire a new generation to discover our history, embrace our heritage and understand the values that help shape our nation’s future,”

Director Madhur Bhandarkar also shared his thoughts on the project and said, “Exploring Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee’s life for the first time as a filmmaker is both a challenge and demanding. Through Syama, I hope to bring an important chapter of India’s history to the screen with honesty, sensitivity and a fresh perspective.”

The film is scheduled to go on floors next year, while further details about the cast and other aspects of the project remain under wraps.

title: Tiger Shroff team shares video of his injuries after Juhu firing incident; actor reportedly sustained cuts and bruises
raw_summary:
Days after a shooting incident of Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu neighbourhood, his team has shared a video on their official social media handle showing the injuries he sustained during the attack. The footage features visible cuts, abrasions and bruises, offering a glimpse of the physical impact of the incident. The actor reportedly escaped direct bullet injuries when unidentified assailants opened fire at his vehicle.

According to the details shared, the injuries were sustained amid the chaos as bullets struck the vehicle and shattered glass. The video shows marks on Tiger’s arms and back. The social media post comes as the investigation into the firing continues, with multiple agencies working to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify everyone allegedly involved.

The shooting took place at around 7 pm on Sunday, October 18, outside a sports facility in Juhu. According to reports, motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at Tiger’s car before fleeing the scene. The two-wheeler was reportedly abandoned near Andheri West railway station.

Tiger Shroff reportedly avoided fatal injuries, while his driver, Firdous, and a passer-by sustained injuries and were taken to Nanavati Hospital. The driver is said to remain under medical observation as he recovers.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Team Tiger Shroff (@teamtigershroff)

Following the incident, an unverified social media claim linked the attack to the Lawrence Bishnoi syndicate. However, the allegation has not been independently established, and investigators are continuing to examine the possible motive and the wider circumstances of the firing.

The Mumbai Crime Branch, working with other law enforcement agencies, has carried out arrests across several states in connection with the case. According to the details provided, the total number of people arrested had reached 10 by October 23.

Three key suspects, identified as Rehan Ansari, Phool Singh and Ritik Mahtoo, were reportedly apprehended in Kota, Rajasthan, while allegedly attempting to flee towards the Nepal border. They were subsequently brought to Mumbai. On October 21, a Mumbai court reportedly remanded the three suspects to police custody until October 31.

Investigators are also examining an alleged interstate weapons network and possible links between those accused of carrying out the attack and individuals suspected of assisting them. Further inquiries are reportedly focused on the planning of the incident, the movement of weapons and the possibility of a wider conspiracy.

The investigation has also prompted renewed scrutiny of security arrangements for prominent Bollywood personalities. Tiger’s representatives have expressed appreciation for the police response and urged people to refrain from circulating unverified information while the investigation remains ongoing.

title: IMA seeks review of Sunny Deol starrer Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak; raises concerns over portrayal of doctors and hospital violence
raw_summary:
The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has raised objections to the promotional content of Sunny Deol’s upcoming crime drama Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, expressing concern over its portrayal of the medical profession. In a formal communication, the association questioned whether the film’s depiction of alleged corruption and violence against healthcare workers could contribute to negative perceptions of doctors and hospital personnel.

The IMA has outlined four key areas of concern, including the generalisation of alleged misconduct across the medical fraternity, the depiction of physical assaults on healthcare workers, the safety of medical personnel and the potential impact on doctor-patient trust.

In its letter, the association cautioned against portraying individual instances of wrongdoing in a manner that could reflect on the wider medical community. It stated, "The portrayal risks creating the impression that corruption, unethical practices, and alleged corruption in medical fraternity. While individual misconduct must be investigated and punished, the actions of a few must not be used to tarnish the reputation of countless honest and dedicated doctors."

The organisation also expressed concern over scenes involving physical confrontations in medical facilities, particularly if such actions are presented as justified. The IMA stated, "Scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff, and hospital personnel, particularly when presented as heroic or justified acts, risk normalising violence against those committed to saving lives."

Highlighting the safety concerns faced by healthcare workers, the association further said, "Doctors and healthcare personnel already face serious safety challenges in hospitals. Content that appears to glorify attacks on medical professionals may encourage hostility and further endanger those providing essential healthcare services."

The IMA also flagged the possible impact of such portrayals on public confidence in medical professionals, stating, "Such portrayals may foster unwarranted mistrust and hostility towards doctors, weakening the mutual trust and cooperation essential for effective treatment and healthcare delivery."

While making its objections known, the association clarified that it does not support unethical medical practices and that individual cases of misconduct should be addressed through statutory and disciplinary mechanisms. It argued that such instances should not lead to broad portrayals that could affect the reputation of the profession or discourage aspiring medical students.

As part of its appeal, the IMA requested an impartial review of the film’s content and asked for appropriate corrective measures to address its concerns. It also called on the relevant authorities to consider further action, stating, "In view of these concerns, we respectfully request... [an] impartial review of the film's content and its portrayal of the medical profession; seek appropriate corrective measures from the filmmakers to address the generalisation of alleged misconduct and the depiction of violence against healthcare workers; [and] consider a ban or other appropriate action if justified under applicable law."

Directed by M. Padmakumar in his Hindi directorial debut, Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak is an official remake of the 2018 Malayalam crime thriller Joseph. The film stars Sunny Deol as a retired police officer who investigates disturbing revelations involving medical malpractice and systemic corruption following a personal tragedy. The supporting cast includes Ravi Kishan, Pragya Jaiswal, Manish Wadhwa and Jisshu Sengupta.

Produced by Kamal Mukut, the film is scheduled to release theatrically on November 20, 2026. The IMA’s objections have brought attention to the film’s portrayal of healthcare workers ahead of its planned release.

Organised under the leadership of Puraskar Thadani, Founder and Editor-in-Chief of ELITE Magazine, the event will recognise Indian achievers and personalities from different industries on an international platform.

Known for his work in Hindi cinema, Karan Johar has established a presence across filmmaking, production and television. As the host of ELITE Most Influential Season VI, he will lead the ceremony, which is expected to bring together individuals recognised for their contributions to business, entertainment, fashion, media and other sectors.

The upcoming edition will be held at the Bodleian Libraries, one of the University of Oxford's historic institutions. The choice of venue continues the event's association with internationally recognised landmarks, providing a global setting for the recognition of achievements across industries.

Puraskar Thadani, who founded the ELITE Most Influential platform, has been associated with its expansion across international locations. Previous editions have been linked to landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower in Paris, Tower Bridge in London, the Statue of Liberty in New York, Burj Khalifa in Dubai and the Museum of the Future. With the University of Oxford hosting the sixth season, the platform will add another prominent international venue to its list.

Known professionally as "Mr. Impossible", Thadani has developed the initiative around recognising individuals for their professional accomplishments and providing them with opportunities for international recognition.

Over the years, ELITE Most Influential has honoured or been associated with personalities from various fields. Its previous honourees and associations include television journalist Rajat Sharma, business leader Indra Nooyi, designer Masaba Gupta, entrepreneur Sabeer Bhatia, industrialist Adi Godrej and actor Vivek Oberoi. The event's previous editions have also had sponsorship and support associations with luxury brands, including Rolls-Royce Motor Cars and Jacob & Co. Watches.

Ghai also has several projects in the pipeline, including Khalnayak Returns with Sanjay Dutt and a courtroom drama featuring Anil Kapoor. Further details about the upcoming projects and their casts are expected to be announced in due course.

Meanwhile, Manya marks Ghai’s reunion with Shreyas Talpade, whom he previously directed in the National Award-winning film Iqbal. Produced by Mukta Arts and Puneet Aggarwal, the film is directed by Sameer Joshi. The heartwarming drama follows a juvenile boy from the slums who turns to theft, exploring his circumstances and journey.

Speaking about Manya, Subhash Ghai said, “Working with Shreyas Talpade for this film has been a wonderful experience. He is an exceptionally versatile actor who has demonstrated his range through films like Iqbal, Apna Sapna Money Money and Golmaal. His performance in this heart shattering drama MANYA has once again reminded me of his ability to bring authenticity and depth to a character. This also marks the beginning of more exciting films together as Mukta Arts moves into another year of its glorious journey.”

For Ghai, the collaboration arrives in a year that marks five decades of his association with Indian cinema. With Manya bringing him back together with Talpade after two decades, the filmmaker is also looking ahead to the next phase of Mukta Arts, with projects spanning films, OTT content and documentaries.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Here’s why Aamir Khan has been mentioned under ‘Special Thanks’ in Prahaar
raw_summary:
Prahaar, which was released on October 16, has been appreciated for its subject, dramatic and emotional moments, award-worthy performances and first-rate direction by Avinash Arun. Moviegoers who watched the film were pleasantly surprised to spot Aamir Khan's name in the 'Special Thanks' section of the credits. Bollywood Hungama exclusively spoke to Avinash Arun to find out the reason behind this special mention.

Avinash Arun told us, “I have thanked him because he got me on board. He suggested my name to Mr Dinesh Vijan.” He added, “He told me, ‘Avinash, I think you'll do justice to this subject and I think you should consider this project’. That motivated me to take up Prahaar.”

Avinash Arun continued, “I am really grateful to him because since my first film Killa (2015), Aamir sir has been following my work. Even after Paatal Lok, he called me.”

Can we expect a collaboration between the two? Avinash replied, “We are discussing a couple of things. So, hopefully, we'll work together soon!”

About Avinash Arun Avinash Arun is a renowned cinematographer as well as a director. A graduate of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, he has worked as a cinematographer on several significant films like Masaan (2015), Drishyam (2015), Madaari (2016), Hichki (2018) and Karwaan (2018).

He made his directorial debut with the acclaimed Marathi film Killa, followed by Three Of Us (2023) and web series like School Of Lies, Paatal Lok and Pritam And Pedro. Interestingly, he also served as the director of photography (DOP) on the projects he directed, although Saurabh Goswami shared the cinematography responsibilities on Season 1 of Paatal Lok. Even in Prahaar, Avinash Arun has donned the dual hats of director and cinematographer.
